xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2630: pan binary not on PATH for operator shells or spawned work agents; pan doctor can't be run to diagnose it

plan.title: pan binary not on PATH for operator shells or spawned work agents; pan doctor can't be run to diagnose it
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: On a source-checkout machine nothing puts `pan` on PATH. npm bin links exist only after `npm install -g` or `npm link`; postinstall and `pan install` never create one. Spawned agents get only the harness binary directory on PATH (src/lib/agents/spawn.ts lines 405-409), so they cannot run `pan done`, `pan task done` or `pan doctor` from their shell. `pan doctor` has no presence check (describeCliGenerationDrift reports ok with 'no global CLI link on this machine'), and the operator cannot run it anyway because `pan` is the missing command.
narratives.Proposal: Add a leaf module src/lib/pan-cli-shim.ts that renders a `/bin/sh` exec shim (`exec '<process.execPath>' '<packageRoot>/dist/cli/index.js' "$@"`, built from panCliInvocation(), plus `export ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` under Electron) into `<OVERDECK_HOME>/cli-bin/{pan,overdeck}`. Every non-remote launcher writes the shim atomically at launch time and prepends that directory to PATH after its extraEnvExports (one line in generateLauncherScript). `pan install` and `pan sync` write the same shim through an async writer, and `pan install` prints the PATH line when `pan` is missing. `pan doctor` gains a `pan on PATH` warn row with three remedies. The source-checkout postinstall prints a one-line hint. The docs cover source-checkout install, the `pan: command not found` bootstrap (`node <checkout>/dist/cli/index.js doctor`) and the launcher PATH line. Full detail: .pan/drafts/PAN-2630.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No `pan doctor --fix`; doctor only reports.
- No automatic `npm link` or `npm install -g` from any Overdeck command.
- No edits to operator shell rc or profile files.
- No change to src/lib/deploy/global-cli-link.ts repoint semantics (PAN-3538).
- Remote (Fly, spawnMode 'remote') launchers must produce the same script as before.
- No edits to src/lib/agents/spawn.ts, including the knowledge-role $HOME/.overdeck/bin PATH line.
- No allowlist cap raise in scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt.
- No shim for the packaged desktop layout where <packageRoot>/dist/cli/index.js does not exist.

autoDecisions.summary: Use one shared shim directory <OVERDECK_HOME>/cli-bin, rewritten by every launcher at launch time.
autoDecisions.rationale: The operator's 2026-11-05 issue comment names this location and asks for spawn-time regeneration, so the shim follows the live reload generation. Per-agent directories need an id some launchers lack and give operators no stable directory to add to PATH.

autoDecisions.summary: Prepend the shim directory after all extraEnvExports, so it precedes the harness binary directory.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue comment says 'after the harness PATH line'. Agents then run the same CLI build as the process that launched them, which also removes PAN-3538-style drift for agents. The directory holds only pan and overdeck, so it shadows nothing else.

autoDecisions.summary: Emit the shim through a single line in generateLauncherScript, not in spawn.ts or each caller.
autoDecisions.rationale: All 15 launcher callers pass through the generator. spawn.ts has 1 line of file-size headroom, and launcher-generator.ts has 3.

autoDecisions.summary: Exec shim with an absolute node path, not a symlink to dist/cli/index.js.
autoDecisions.rationale: The bundle's `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang depends on whichever node is on PATH, and a symlink cannot carry the Electron flag.

autoDecisions.summary: Bake `export ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` into the shim when process.versions.electron is set or the generating process has ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 at render time.
autoDecisions.rationale: In the desktop app process.execPath is Electron. Without the flag the shim relaunches the desktop app (PAN-2559 fork-bomb). A Herdr pane does not inherit the server's env.

autoDecisions.summary: Atomic best-effort shim writes (tmp file with $$, chmod, mv -f), guarded by [ -f <bundle> ]; on failure skip the PATH export and never exit.
autoDecisions.rationale: Many launchers write the shared file concurrently, and a launcher must never die because of a convenience shim.
Fly VMs have their own install and the host's absolute paths are invalid there.

autoDecisions.summary: The doctor `pan on PATH` row is warn, not error, and lists npm install -g, npm link, and the cli-bin PATH line.
autoDecisions.rationale: Agents no longer depend on the operator's PATH. The comment asks for a warning with the npm install -g / npm link fix text; the cli-bin line is the third remedy the shim makes possible.

autoDecisions.summary: Add a one-line postinstall hint, only in source checkouts (<PACKAGE_ROOT>/src exists) and only when no pan is on PATH.
autoDecisions.rationale: `bun install` is the first command a source-checkout operator runs, which breaks the 'diagnosis tool is the missing tool' circularity. Published installs ship no src/, so npm install -g stays silent.

metadata.sizeJustification: Seven small vertical items across one new module, the launcher generator, three CLI commands, a script and docs. All belong to one PATH guarantee and none ships value alone.

items.title: Add src/lib/pan-cli-shim.ts: shim renderer, launcher lines, async writer, PATH lookup

narrative.Action:
Create the new leaf module src/lib/pan-cli-shim.ts beside src/lib/pan-cli-invocation.ts, exactly as PRD WI-1 specifies. It imports only node:path, node:fs, node:fs/promises, ./paths.js (getOverdeckHome), ./shell-quote.js (shellQuote) and ./pan-cli-invocation.js (panCliInvocation). Export PanCliShimRuntime {nodePath?, root?, electron?, dir?} and these functions: panCliShimDir() = join(getOverdeckHome(), 'cli-bin'), read at call time; panCliBundlePath(runtime) = panCliInvocation([], {nodePath, root}).args[0]; renderPanCliShim(runtime), which returns exactly "#!/bin/sh
" + (electron ? "export ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1
" : "") + "exec <shellQuote(node)> <shellQuote(bundle)> "$@"
", with electron defaulting to Boolean(process.versions.electron) || process.env.ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE === '1'; panCliShimLauncherLines(runtime), which returns bash lines that, only when `[ -f <bundle> ]`, mkdir -p the dir, write the renderPanCliShim() content through a quoted heredoc (delimiter OVERDECK_PAN_SHIM) to <dir>/pan.tmp.$$, chmod 0755, copy it to <dir>/overdeck.tmp.$$, mv -f both into place, then `export PATH=<shellQuote(dir)>:"$PATH"`. Any failure skips the export, the tmp files are removed on every path, and the whole block is one compound `if` that never exits the launcher. Also export writePanCliShims(runtime): Promise<{status:'written',dir}|{status:'missing-bundle',bundle}|{status:'error',message}>. It is async fs/promises, checks the bundle exists, writes each file to a randomUUID tmp with mode 0o755, renames it, and never throws. Finally export findExecutableOnPath(name, pathEnv, deps?): a pure split of pathEnv on ':' that skips empty segments and returns the first join(segment,name) where deps.isExecutableFile (default: statSync().isFile() plus accessSync X_OK in a try/catch) is true, else null. Add a header comment naming PAN-2630 and the D-1/D-3/D-4/D-6 reasoning. Write tests/unit/lib/pan-cli-shim.test.ts with the five cases listed in PRD WI-1. Use mkdtemp fixtures, and use spawnSync('bash', ['-c', ...]) to execute the launcher lines against a fake bundle that prints JSON.stringify(process.argv.slice(2)).

items.title: Given nodePath '/n/node' and root '/r', renderPanCliShim returns exactly "#!/bin/sh\nexec '/n/node' '/r/dist/cli/index.js' \"$@\"\n", and with electron: true it emits `export ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` as line 2

Given a temp root with a fake dist/cli/index.js, when bash executes panCliShimLauncherLines() followed by `command -v pan; pan a "b c"`, then it exits 0, prints <dir>/pan, prints ["a","b c"], and leaves no *.tmp.* file in the dir
Given a root without dist/cli/index.js, when bash executes the launcher lines, then it exits 0, creates no pan file, and the printed PATH does not contain the shim dir
writePanCliShims() creates pan and overdeck with mode 0o755 and content equal to renderPanCliShim(), and returns {status:'missing-bundle'} and writes nothing when the bundle is absent
findExecutableOnPath('pan', '/a::/b', {isExecutableFile: p => p === '/b/pan'}) returns '/b/pan', and returns null for no match and for an undefined PATH
Emit the pan shim block in generateLauncherScript after extraEnvExports for non-remote launchers

narrative.Action: In src/lib/launcher-generator.ts add exactly two lines (the file is 997 of 1000 lines, so add no blank line and no comment). First, `import { panCliShimLauncherLines } from './pan-cli-shim.js';` among the './' imports. Second, directly after the closing brace of the `// Extra env exports` block (`if (config.extraEnvExports) { for (const expr of config.extraEnvExports) { lines.push(expr); } }`, lines 392-397), add `if (config.spawnMode !== 'remote') lines.push(...panCliShimLauncherLines());`. Do not touch src/lib/agents/spawn.ts. In src/lib/__tests__/launcher-generator.test.ts add a local normalize(script) helper that replaces tempHome with '<OVERDECK_HOME>', process.execPath with '<NODE>', and packageRoot (import from '../paths.js') with '<PACKAGE_ROOT>'. Use it in place of every `script.replaceAll(tempHome, '<OVERDECK_HOME>')`, then regenerate the inline snapshots with `npx vitest run src/lib/__tests__/launcher-generator.test.ts -u` and confirm each non-remote snapshot shows the shim block after the extra env exports. Create tests/unit/lib/launcher-generator-pan-shim.test.ts. In it, vi.mock the pan-cli-invocation module so that panCliInvocation(args) returns {command: process.execPath, args: [<tmp>/dist/cli/index.js, ...args]} for a fake bundle, set OVERDECK_HOME to a temp dir, and generate a launcher with extraEnvExports ["export PATH='/harness/bin':\"$PATH\""] and baseCommand 'printenv PATH; command -v pan'. Write it to disk, run it with spawnSync('bash', [path]), and assert the PATH order and pan resolution. Add a second case: a spawnMode 'remote' launcher contains no 'cli-bin'.

pan install writes the pan shim and prints the PATH line when pan is missing

narrative.Action: In src/cli/commands/install.ts export `async function installPanCliShimStep(deps: { write: typeof writePanCliShims; find: typeof findExecutableOnPath; pathEnv: string | undefined; log: (line: string) => void }): Promise<void>`. It calls deps.write(). On {status:'written', dir} it logs a green `✓ pan shim written to <dir>`; then, if deps.find('pan', deps.pathEnv) returns null, it logs a yellow `pan is not on your PATH. Add this to your shell profile: export PATH="<dir>:$PATH"`. On 'missing-bundle' or 'error' it logs a yellow warning with the reason and returns normally (never exits non-zero, never throws). In installCommand, directly after `await setupHooksCommand();` (line 284), call `await installPanCliShimStep({ write: writePanCliShims, find: findExecutableOnPath, pathEnv: process.env.PATH, log: (l) => console.log(l) })`. Write tests/unit/cli/install-pan-shim.test.ts covering written+missing, written+present and error, with injected fakes.

items.title: Given write returns {status:'written', dir:'/d'} and find returns null, installPanCliShimStep logs a line containing `export PATH="/d:$PATH"`
Given write returns written and find returns '/usr/bin/pan', installPanCliShimStep logs no line containing 'export PATH'

Given write returns {status:'error', message:'EACCES'}, installPanCliShimStep resolves without throwing and logs a warning containing 'EACCES'; installCommand calls the step right after setupHooksCommand()

narrative.Action: In src/cli/commands/sync.ts export `async function syncPanCliShimStep(deps: { write: typeof writePanCliShims; log: (line: string) => void }): Promise<void>`. It logs exactly one line: dim `pan shim → <dir>` on written, yellow `pan shim not written: bundle missing at <bundle>` on missing-bundle, and yellow `pan shim not written: <message>` on error. It never throws. In syncCommand, just before the `// Sync statusline to all runtimes` block (around line 543), add `if (!options.dryRun) await timeAsync('sync-pan-shim', () => syncPanCliShimStep({ write: writePanCliShims, log: (l) => console.log(l) }));`. Write tests/unit/cli/sync-pan-shim.test.ts covering the three statuses with an injected writer.

items.title: Given write returns {status:'written', dir:'/d'}, syncPanCliShimStep logs exactly one line, and it contains '/d'
Given write returns missing-bundle or error, syncPanCliShimStep resolves without throwing and logs exactly one line starting with 'pan shim not written'
syncCommand calls syncPanCliShimStep only when options.dryRun is falsy, so `pan sync --dry-run` writes no shim
pan doctor reports a 'pan on PATH' row (warn with three remedies when missing)

narrative.Action: Create src/cli/commands/doctor-pan-path.ts shaped like src/cli/commands/doctor-cli-generation.ts, and re-declare CheckResult locally to avoid the module cycle. Export `checkPanOnPath(deps: { pathEnv?: string; find?: typeof findExecutableOnPath; shimDir?: string } = {}): CheckResult`. Defaults: process.env.PATH, findExecutableOnPath, panCliShimDir(). When pan is found, return {name:'pan on PATH', status:'ok', message:<resolved path>}, and append ' (Overdeck shim)' when the path equals join(shimDir,'pan'). When it is missing, return {name:'pan on PATH', status:'warn', message:`pan is not on PATH in this shell (agents get it from ${shimDir})`, fix:`Run npm install -g @overdeck/core, or npm link inside your Overdeck checkout after npm run build, or add export PATH="${shimDir}:$PATH" to your shell profile (pan sync writes that shim)`}. Spawn no child process and call no execSync. Register it in src/cli/commands/doctor.ts with one import line beside `import { checkCliGenerationLink } from './doctor-cli-generation.js';` (line 25), and by changing line 787 to `checks.push(await checkCliGenerationLink(), checkPanOnPath());`. Do not change describeCliGenerationDrift in src/lib/deploy/global-cli-link.ts. Write tests/unit/cli/doctor-pan-path.test.ts with injected find and pathEnv.

items.title: Given find returns null, checkPanOnPath returns status 'warn' whose fix contains 'npm install -g @overdeck/core', 'npm link' and 'export PATH="<shimDir>:$PATH"'
Given find returns <shimDir>/pan, checkPanOnPath returns status 'ok' with a message ending in '(Overdeck shim)'; given find returns '/usr/local/bin/pan', the message equals '/usr/local/bin/pan'
doctor.ts pushes checkPanOnPath() in the same checks.push call as checkCliGenerationLink(), so `pan doctor` output renders a 'pan on PATH' row
Source-checkout postinstall prints a hint when pan is not on PATH

narrative.Action: In scripts/postinstall.mjs add `function hintMissingPan()` and call it before `syncHooksIfInitialized();`. It returns immediately unless existsSync(join(PACKAGE_ROOT, 'src')) holds, which is the source-checkout signal; published tarballs ship no src/. Otherwise it scans (process.env.PATH || '').split(':') and skips empty segments. For each segment it tests join(segment, 'pan') with statSync(...).isFile() plus accessSync(..., constants.X_OK) inside a try/catch, with no child process. If none matches it prints exactly one line: `Overdeck: pan is not on your PATH. After npm run build, run npm link in this checkout, or add ~/.overdeck/cli-bin to PATH after pan install. Until then: node dist/cli/index.js doctor`. Keep the existing behavior and the `|| true` exit semantics in package.json. Write tests/unit/scripts/postinstall-pan-hint.test.ts. Run spawnSync(process.execPath, [join(process.cwd(),'scripts','postinstall.mjs')]) with env HOME=<temp dir> (so ~/.overdeck is absent) and PATH=<dirname(process.execPath)>, and assert stdout contains 'pan is not on your PATH'. Then rerun with PATH=<temp dir holding an executable `pan` file>:<dirname(process.execPath)> and assert it does not.

narrative.Action: Edit exactly the files in PRD WI-7. (1) docs/USAGE.md: under `## Installation` add `### From a source checkout` with the steps git clone, bun install, npm run build, then npm link, or alternatively `node dist/cli/index.js install` followed by adding `export PATH="$HOME/.overdeck/cli-bin:$PATH"` to the shell profile. State that agents launched by Overdeck get pan from ~/.overdeck/cli-bin automatically. (2) docs/BUILD.md: add `## Running the CLI from a checkout` after the Build Commands table, describing the pan/overdeck exec shim in ~/.overdeck/cli-bin, what writes it (every non-remote launcher, pan install, pan sync), and that it runs the writer's node binary by absolute path. (3) reference/troubleshooting.mdx: add `## pan: command not found` before `## WSL2 Stability Issues (Windows Users)`. Give the bootstrap command `node <your-checkout>/dist/cli/index.js doctor`, explain the 'pan on PATH' doctor row, and list the three remedies (npm install -g @overdeck/core; npm link in the checkout after npm run build; export PATH="$HOME/.overdeck/cli-bin:$PATH"). (4) docs/TERMINAL-BACKENDS.md: next to the sentence 'The launcher exports `OVERDECK_AGENT_ID` on Herdr' (around line 337), add one sentence: every non-remote launcher writes the pan shim to ~/.overdeck/cli-bin and puts that directory first on PATH (PAN-2630). (5) .overdeck/context/codebase/architecture.md: add a bullet after the `agent-tmpdir.ts` bullet: `pan-cli-shim.ts` — the pan/overdeck exec shim in <OVERDECK_HOME>/cli-bin that every non-remote launcher writes and puts first on PATH; pan install and pan sync write it too (PAN-2630). Leave its last-verified line unchanged. Follow the repo's plain STE writing style.
